hints: The speed between two nodes is the smallest edge on their tree path.
Process edges from largest speed down.
When components of sizes a and b join at speed w, exactly a*b new pairs have bottleneck w.
analogy: As the speed threshold falls, newly connected pairs acquire the threshold as their route speed.
example: For a path with edge speeds 5 and 2, the three pair speeds are 5,2,2, summing to 9.
algorithm: Sort tree edges by decreasing speed. Maintain components and their sizes with disjoint-set union. Before joining an edge of speed w connecting components of sizes a and b, add w*a*b to the answer, then merge them. Use wide integer arithmetic.
correctness: When an edge of speed w is processed, all edges already used have speed at least w. Every newly joined pair has a path containing this edge and no smaller edge, so its bottleneck is w; each pair is counted exactly once.
complexity: For n nodes, O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
